source: Curated for Saptarushi. Story and significance follow the traditional accounts; coordinates are approximate for map markers.

items.name: Shankari Devi Temple
items.bodyPart: Traditions differ on the associated body part.
items.story: Shankari Devi is traditionally associated with the Shakti Peetha at Trincomalee. The Shakti Peetha tradition connects these sacred places with the story of Sati and the cosmic intervention of Shiva after her self-immolation.
items.significance: The shrine represents one of the great sacred seats of the Divine Mother and connects Indian Shakta tradition with the sacred geography of Sri Lanka.

items.name: Kamakshi Amman Temple
items.story: Kamakshi is revered as the supreme Divine Mother at Kanchipuram. The temple is deeply connected with the Sri Vidya tradition and the sacred heritage of Kanchi.
items.significance: Kamakshi is one of the most important forms of Devi worship in South India, and Kanchipuram is one of India's major temple cities.

items.name: Chamundeshwari Temple
items.story: Chamundeshwari is traditionally identified with the Goddess who defeated the buffalo demon Mahishasura. The deity became deeply associated with the royal and religious heritage of Mysuru.
items.significance: The hilltop temple is one of the most recognizable sacred landmarks of Mysuru.

items.name: Jogulamba Temple
items.story: Jogulamba is revered as a powerful form of Goddess Shakti. Alampur has long been an important Shaiva-Shakta sacred centre.
items.significance: The temple forms an important part of the sacred geography around the Tungabhadra and Krishna river region.

items.name: Bhramaramba Temple
items.story: Bhramaramba is traditionally associated with the Divine Mother at Srisailam and is worshipped together with Mallikarjuna Shiva.
items.significance: Srisailam is especially significant because the same sacred complex is associated with both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha tradition.

items.name: Mahalakshmi Temple
items.story: The Mahalakshmi tradition at Kolhapur is one of the great centres of Goddess worship in Maharashtra.
items.significance: The temple is one of the most important pilgrimage centres in western India.

items.name: Mahakali / Harsiddhi Temple
items.story: Ujjain is one of India's great sacred cities. The Mahakali tradition is associated with the city's ancient Shaiva and Shakta heritage.
items.significance: The temple stands within one of India's most important pilgrimage landscapes.

items.name: Puruhutika Devi Temple
items.story: Pithapuram is an important pilgrimage centre and is traditionally associated with Puruhutika Devi.
items.significance: The shrine forms part of Andhra Pradesh's rich Shakta and Shaiva pilgrimage network.

items.name: Biraja Temple
items.story: Biraja Devi is worshipped at the ancient sacred centre of Jajpur, traditionally associated with the Shakti Peetha tradition.
items.significance: Jajpur's sacred landscape is closely connected with the Vaitarani river and ancient Odishan religious history.

items.name: Manikyamba Temple
items.story: Manikyamba is revered at Draksharamam, one of the great Shaiva centres of Andhra Pradesh.
items.significance: The site is particularly important because Draksharamam is also one of the five Pancharama Kshetras.

items.name: Kamakhya Temple
items.story: Kamakhya is one of the most important Shakta pilgrimage centres in India and is strongly associated with Tantric traditions.
items.significance: The temple is a major centre of Shakti worship and the annual Ambubachi Mela is particularly significant.

items.name: Madhaveshwari / Alopi Devi
items.story: Prayagraj's sacred geography centres around the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and traditionally revered Saraswati.
items.significance: The city is one of India's most important pilgrimage destinations.

items.name: Jwalamukhi Temple
items.story: Jwalamukhi is famous for its sacred flames, which are traditionally revered as manifestations of the Goddess.
items.significance: The shrine is particularly distinctive because worship centres around naturally occurring flames rather than a conventional anthropomorphic idol.

items.name: Mangala Gauri Temple
items.story: Gaya is one of India's ancient pilgrimage centres, particularly important for ancestral rites.
items.significance: Mangala Gauri forms an important part of the sacred geography of Gaya.

items.name: Vishalakshi Temple
items.story: Vishalakshi is one of the important Devi shrines within the sacred city of Varanasi.
items.significance: The temple is closely associated with the wider Kashi pilgrimage circuit.

items.name: Tara Devi Temple
items.location: Tarapith, Birbhum district, West Bengal, India
items.story: Tarapith is a major centre of Shakta worship connected with the fierce form of the Divine Mother as Tara, deeply linked with the saint Sadhak Bamakhepa. The shrine stands near the river Dwarka in the Birbhum landscape.
items.significance: Tarapith is one of the most important Tara-Peetha shrines of eastern India and a living centre of esoteric Shakta sadhana.

items.name: Vimala Temple
items.bodyPart: Traditionally associated with the feet of Sati.
items.story: Inside the Jagannath complex at Puri, Goddess Vimala is revered together with Lord Jagannath. The shakti of Jagannath is considered to rest here, so the Bhoga (offering) is first served to Vimala Devi.
items.significance: Puri is thus a unique site where a Char Dham shrine and a Shakti Peetha tradition exist within a single temple complex.

items.name: Ambaji Temple
items.bodyPart: Traditionally associated with the heart of Sati.
items.story: The Ambaji shrine on Gabbar hill is one of the principal Shakti Peethas of western India. The idol is worshipped without a physical image, on a sacred Ċhorasi-chamakī symbol associated with the mother.
items.significance: Ambaji is a major centre of the Gujarati Shakta tradition and a destination of the Arasuri fair.

items.name: Somnath Jyotirlinga
items.location: Prabhas Patan, Gir Somnath district, Gujarat
items.story: According to tradition, Chandra, the Moon God, worshipped Shiva at Prabhas to obtain relief from a curse associated with Daksha.
items.significance: Somnath is traditionally regarded as the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas and occupies an important place in India's religious and historical memory.

items.name: Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga
items.story: Mallikarjuna is traditionally associated with Shiva at Sri Shaila. The temple is connected with the story of Shiva and Parvati and the sacred Nallamala hills.
items.significance: It is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and the same sacred complex is associated with Bhramaramba.

items.name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
items.story: Mahakaleshwar represents Shiva as Mahakala, the Lord beyond time.
items.significance: The temple is especially famous for the Bhasma Aarti and is one of India's most important Shaiva pilgrimage sites.

items.name: Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga
items.location: Mandhata Island, Narmada River, Madhya Pradesh
items.story: Omkareshwar is traditionally associated with Shiva's manifestation on the sacred island in the Narmada.
items.significance: The island is traditionally described as resembling the sacred syllable Om.

items.name: Baidyanath Jyotirlinga
items.story: The Vaidyanath tradition connects Shiva with the healing aspect of the divine.
items.significance: Deoghar is the most commonly represented modern location in many Jyotirlinga pilgrimage lists, although Parli in Maharashtra also has a traditional claim.

items.name: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga
items.story: Bhimashankar is associated with traditions surrounding Shiva's battle with the demon Bhima.
items.significance: The temple lies within the Sahyadri landscape and is also associated with the origin of the Bhima river.

items.name: Ramanathaswamy Jyotirlinga
items.story: The temple is deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition and the worship of Shiva by Rama.
items.significance: The temple is renowned for its immense corridors and occupies a major place in South Indian pilgrimage.

items.name: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga
items.location: Near Dwarka, Devbhumi Dwarka district, Gujarat
items.story: Nageshwar is associated with Shiva as the Lord connected with serpents and protection.
items.significance: The temple forms part of the important Dwarka pilgrimage circuit.

items.name: Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga
items.story: Kashi is one of the oldest continuously revered sacred cities in India, and Vishwanath is regarded as Shiva as Lord of the Universe.
items.significance: The temple is one of the most important Shaiva pilgrimage destinations in India.

items.name: Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga
items.story: Trimbakeshwar is closely associated with the origin of the Godavari and ancient Shaiva traditions.
items.significance: The shrine is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and an important pilgrimage destination near Nashik.

items.name: Kedarnath Jyotirlinga
items.story: Kedarnath is traditionally associated with the Pandavas and Shiva's manifestation in the Himalayas.
items.significance: Kedarnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas and one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites of Uttarakhand.

items.name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga
items.story: The Grishneshwar tradition celebrates Shiva through a story of devotion and divine grace.
items.significance: Its proximity to the Ellora cave complex makes it especially important within the heritage landscape of Maharashtra.

items.name: Amararama
items.story: Amararama is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras associated with the sacred lingam of the Tarakasura tradition.
items.significance: It is one of the principal Shaiva pilgrimage temples of Andhra Pradesh.

items.name: Draksharama
items.story: Draksharama is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras and is traditionally associated with Bhimeswara Shiva.
items.significance: The site is especially important because Draksharama is also traditionally counted as a Shakti Peetha through Manikyamba.

items.name: Somarama
items.story: Somarama is traditionally included among the five Pancharama Shiva temples.
items.significance: It forms an important part of the regional Shaiva pilgrimage circuit.

items.name: Ksheerarama
items.story: Ksheerarama is one of the five Pancharama Kshetras of Andhra Pradesh.
items.significance: The temple is an important Shaiva centre in the Godavari region.

items.name: Kumararama (Bhimaramam)
items.story: Kumararama is traditionally included among the five Pancharama Kshetras.
items.significance: It is an important Shaiva temple in the Kakinada region.

items.name: Badrinath Dham
items.story: Badrinath is traditionally associated with Vishnu in the Himalayas, seated in meditation above the Alaknanda river. It is counted among the Char Dham and the Utharayan pilgrimage circuit.
items.significance: One of the most revered Vaishnava shrines in the Indian Himalayas.

items.name: Dwarkadhish Dham
items.story: Dwarka is traditionally identified as Krishna's capital in the Mahabharata, and the Dwarkadhish temple is one of the Char Dham, saluted as Jagat Mandir.
items.significance: A principal Krishna pilgrimage site on the western coast of India.

items.name: Jagannath Dham (Puri)
items.story: Puri's Jagannath temple is a Char Dham site where Krishna is worshipped with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra. The annual Ratha Yatra is famous worldwide.
items.significance: One of the four cardinal pilgrimage destinations of Hindu India.

items.name: Rameswaram Dham
items.story: Rameswaram, traditionally part of the Ramayana landscape, completes the southern Char Dham. Its Shiva temple is closely linked with Rama's worship at the close of his expedition.
items.significance: Often counted as one of the Char Dham, making the four sites circle the whole of India.

items.name: Ekambareswarar Temple
items.story: Ekambareswarar is the earth (Prithvi) element sthal and the largest temple in Kanchipuram, dated by tradition to the Pallava era.
items.significance: One of the five Pancha Bhoota temples and part of Kanchipuram's ancient temple landscape.

items.name: Thiruvanaikaval Jambukeswarar
items.story: The Jambukeswarar temple is the water element (Appu) sthal and is intertwined with the legend of the sage Valmiki and an elephant's daily worship of a lingam beneath a jambu tree.
items.significance: One of the five Pancha Bhoota temples, set within the Srirangam island landscape.

items.name: Arunachaleswarar Temple
items.story: Tiruvannamalai is the fire element (Agni) sthal. According to the tradition of the origin of the lingam, Shiva stood as a column of flame on the Arunachala hill, and the temple now crowns its foot.
items.significance: One of the five Pancha Bhoota temples, famous for the Karthigai Deepam festival.

items.name: Srikalahasti Temple
items.story: Srikalahasti is the Vayu sthal of the five Pancha Bhoota temples, where the deity is worshipped in the form of air. The ancient legend of the spider, snake and elephant is the source of the name Kalahasti.
items.significance: One of the Pancha Bhoota Shiva temples; also a renowned centre of Vemana and Vastu tradition.

items.name: Thillai Nataraja Temple
items.story: Chidambaram is the space (Aakasha) element sthal. The temple is renowned for its worship of Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance, symbolising the cosmos in motion.
items.significance: One of the five Pancha Bhoota temples and a great centre of Shaiva Siddhanta and Bharatanatyam.
